name: EU Cyber Resilience Act — Annex I

preConditions.label: Product includes digital elements
preConditions.description: Checks that the product includes digital elements. Gates all CRA Annex I obligations — only products with digital elements are in scope.

preConditions.label: Product allows user configuration
preConditions.description: Checks that the product can be configured by the user. Gates the secure-by-default obligation, which only applies to configurable products.

preConditions.label: Product restricts access
preConditions.description: Checks that the product restricts access to authorised users. Gates the access control obligation, which only applies to products that enforce access control.

preConditions.label: Product processes or stores data
preConditions.description: Checks that the product processes or stores data. Gates the encryption and data minimisation obligations, which only apply to products that handle data.

preConditions.label: Product uses external services
preConditions.description: Checks that the product relies on external or third-party services. Gates the external service resilience obligation, which only applies to products with external integrations.

preConditions.label: Product exposes a digital interface
preConditions.description: Checks that the product exposes a digital interface (network API, communication endpoint). Gates the attack surface limitation obligation, which only applies to products with exposed interfaces.

preConditions.label: Product has available security updates
preConditions.description: Checks that the product currently offers security updates to users. Gates the public disclosure and free update distribution obligations, which only apply when updates exist.

obligations.label: Product ensures appropriate cybersecurity level
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §1. Products with digital elements shall ensure an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks. Checks that the product's cybersecurity level meets or exceeds the applicable regulatory threshold.

obligations.label: Product has no known exploitable vulnerabilities
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §2. Products with digital elements shall be delivered without any known exploitable vulnerabilities. Checks that all published security advisories have associated patch versions, confirming all disclosed vulnerabilities have been remediated.

obligations.label: Product ships with secure default configuration
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(a). Products shall be deployable and usable in a secure configuration. Checks that the product ships with secure defaults and does not include hardcoded default passwords.

obligations.label: Product enforces access control
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(b). Products that restrict access shall implement appropriate access control mechanisms. Checks that the product enforces strong authentication by default and supports scoped access tokens to limit privilege.

obligations.label: Product encrypts data
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(c). Products that process or store data shall protect confidentiality by encrypting data at rest and in transit. Checks that the product implements encrypted transport and storage mechanisms.

obligations.label: Product protects data and software integrity
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(d). Products shall protect the integrity of stored, transmitted or processed data, commands and configurations against unauthorised modification. Checks that cryptographic signing mechanisms are in place for software artefacts.

obligations.label: Product minimises data collection
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(e). Products that process data shall collect only data adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary. Checks that data collection is opt-in by default.

obligations.label: Product preserves availability of essential functions
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(f). Products shall protect the availability of their essential functions, including resilience against denial-of-service attacks. Checks that the product provides built-in availability or automatic recovery mechanisms.

obligations.label: Product resists external service disruption
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(g). Products shall minimise their negative impact on the availability of services provided by other devices or networks they depend on. Checks that the product continues operating essential functions when external services are unavailable.

obligations.label: Product limits its attack surface
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(h). Products shall be designed to limit attack surfaces, including external interfaces. Checks that the number of exposed network integration endpoints remains within acceptable bounds.

obligations.label: Product applies exploitation mitigations
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(i). Products shall reduce the impact of incidents using appropriate exploitation mitigation techniques. Checks that the product targets a runtime providing OS-level mitigations such as ASLR and DEP.

obligations.label: Product logs security events
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(j). Products shall provide security information by recording and monitoring relevant internal activity, including access to or modification of data, services or functions. Checks that the product includes a security event logging component.

obligations.label: Product supports security updates
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part I, §3(k). Products shall ensure that vulnerabilities can be addressed through security updates. Checks that the product has a release mechanism through which users can receive and apply updates.

obligations.label: Manufacturer documents vulnerabilities and components
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part II, §1. Manufacturers shall identify and document vulnerabilities and components in their products, including by drawing up a software bill of materials (SBOM). Checks that an SBOM is publicly available for the product.

obligations.label: Manufacturer remediates vulnerabilities without delay
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part II, §2. Manufacturers shall address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, including by providing security updates. Checks that all disclosed vulnerabilities have associated patch versions applied.

obligations.label: Manufacturer tests security regularly
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part II, §3. Manufacturers shall apply effective and regular testing and reviews of the security of their products. Checks that automated security scanning is integrated into the development pipeline.

obligations.label: Manufacturer discloses fixed vulnerabilities publicly
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part II, §4. Once a security update is available, manufacturers shall publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities. Checks that all published advisories carry CVE identifiers, enabling public disclosure through the NVD.

obligations.label: Manufacturer enforces a disclosure policy
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part II, §5. Manufacturers shall put in place and enforce a policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure. Checks that a SECURITY.md file is accessible at the organisation or repository level.

obligations.label: Manufacturer shares vulnerability information
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part II, §6. Manufacturers shall facilitate sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities with relevant stakeholders. Checks that all published advisories carry CVE identifiers to enable cross-referencing by downstream manufacturers.

obligations.label: Manufacturer distributes updates securely
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part II, §7. Manufacturers shall provide mechanisms to securely distribute updates. Checks that release assets are accompanied by cryptographic signatures (.sig, .asc or .sigstore).

obligations.label: Manufacturer provides free and timely security updates
obligations.description: CRA Annex I, Part II, §8. Manufacturers shall ensure that security updates are provided free of charge and without delay. Checks that the product uses an open-source licence and that the release cadence does not exceed 90 days between updates.
